entities.name: Ngawang Jigme Drakpa
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ngawang Jigme Drakpa (Ngag dbang 'jigs med grags pa) was the final ruling prince of Tsang from the Rinpungpa dynasty, whose reign marked the twilight of a significant regional power in Central Tibet during the mid-16th century. Born into a lineage that had dominated much of Tsang (western Central Tibet) since the late 15th century, he inherited a fragile state increasingly beset by internal dissent and the burgeoning power of rival factions. His rule, which effectively concluded in 1565, represents a pivotal moment in Tibetan political history, transitioning from the Rinpungpa's Sakya-aligned influence to the ascendancy of the Tsangpa dynasty, who were staunch patrons of the Karma Kagyu school.

Drakpa's period of governance was characterized by escalating instability, a stark contrast to the Rinpungpa's earlier dominance. The dynasty, once a formidable force, found its authority eroded by the ambitions of its former vassals, particularly the Tsangpa regime led by Karma Tseten. In 1565, Karma Tseten's forces decisively defeated the Rinpungpa, seizing their principal strongholds, including Rinpung itself, and effectively dismantling their territorial control. This military defeat stripped Ngawang Jigme Drakpa of his temporal power, although he lived until 1597, dedicating his later years to scholarly pursuits.

Beyond his political role, Ngawang Jigme Drakpa was a distinguished scholar and author, contributing significantly to Tibetan literature and historiography. His most notable work, the 'History of the Rinpungpa' (Rin spungs pa'i rgyal rabs), provides invaluable insights into his dynasty's rise and fall, offering a unique perspective from a participant observer. The collapse of the Rinpungpa under his leadership paved the way for the Tsangpa's consolidation of power across Central Tibet, a precursor to the eventual establishment of the Ganden Phodrang government under the Dalai Lamas with Mongol backing in the 17th century.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ngawang Jigme Drakpa's demise as the last Rinpungpa ruler marked the definitive end of a century-long dynastic power in Central Tibet, directly enabling the rise of the Tsangpa regime which dominated the region for the next 60 years. His personal historical writings also provide crucial primary source material for understanding 16th-century Tibetan political and cultural life.
